what_it_does: Industrial sensors often measure tiny voltage differences (millivolts) in the presence of large, unwanted background voltage offsets (up to 24 volts). This paper describes an instrumentation amplifier—a specialized analog circuit—that can handle both the tiny signal and the large offset simultaneously while running on a 36-volt power supply. The key innovation is a current-balancing architecture that keeps the signal very clean (rejecting common-mode interference at 140 dB—meaning it rejects roughly 100 million times better than a naive approach). This level of performance works across all gain settings and bandwidth speeds, making it practical for industrial applications like load cells, thermocouples, and sensor bridges.
